metaDescription: Welsh Terrier vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so Welsh Terrier boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Plan Welsh Terrier social milestones around the schedule rows, not the other way around, because the 16-week finish is the usual green light clinics cite for broader Welsh Terrier exposure.
Weight range 20 lb (9 kg) and grooming needs (Wire coat.) belong in the same Welsh Terrier household ops list as vaccine dates when busy weeks collide.
If your Welsh Terrier is also monitored for allergy skin disease, ask whether bloodwork or orthopedic checks can share a visit with a booster to cut missed Welsh Terrier appointments.
After the Welsh Terrier puppy/kitten series, keep adult DA2PP / DHPP and rabies renewals on 7/3/1-day reminders so year-two surprises disappear.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Owners postpone Welsh Terrier shots when the puppy seems “a little off,” travel intervenes, or primary lens luxation risk worries dominate the week — ask the clinic whether a same-week Welsh Terrier make-up is still appropriate instead of sliding to the annual exam.
Long gaps can leave Welsh Terrier antibody levels uncertain, so expect either an added booster or a titer conversation rather than a shrug.
Do not trade the missed Welsh Terrier dose for extra socialization; finish immunity first for this small dog.
Reset the Welsh Terrier reminder stack the evening of the make-up appointment — including the eventual adult booster after the 16-week finish.

faqs.question: When does the Welsh Terrier core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Welsh Terrier misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Welsh Terrier health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Welsh Terrier adult health guide for breed predispositions such as primary lens luxation risk, then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
